A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark and Learnable Calibration methods. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, adapter ablations, scaling and domain-shift experiments, three-task evaluations, qualitative examples, and learning curves.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Table 2 and Appendices C-H.

M1.justification: Both retain the same adapter merging, bias-vector calibration, low-rank Calibration++ variant, cross-entropy training, and parameter-sharing options. V2's compute-and-load deployment description explains the existing procedure rather than introducing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both use DialogSum, Synthetic Persona Chat, TED Talks, and Sound Natural, with the same languages, tones, and task combinations. SAMSum generalization and three-task composition remain present, moving from Section 5.3 to Appendices E-F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in every corresponding experiment, including TIES, DARE, LoraHub, LM-Cocktail, DAM/ZipLoRA, and the multi-step and joint-expert baselines. V2 clarifies which comparators use compositional data without adding or removing evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, model configurations, training settings, the 10,000-example calibration subset, metrics, and LLM-judge prompts are unchanged. The added prompt and baseline-data explanations disclose details without reporting revised experimental settings.

E4.justification: Parameter-sharing and adapter-removal ablations, weight analyses, scaling, domain generalization, three-task evaluations, qualitative cases, and learning curves are retained. V2 reorganizes existing analyses into Appendices D-H without adding or removing analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both report the same averaging across models and languages or tones. Neither introduces experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Corresponding table values, plotted results, and qualitative outputs match. For example, Table 2 reports Calibration++ summarization-plus-translation scores of 28.64 ROUGE-L and 65.15 LLM-J in both. V1 Tables 5-6 become v2 Tables A3-A4 with unchanged results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(7), including task composition and both calibration formulas, retain the same mathematics. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: on-device compositional multi-tasking, a four-task benchmark, and efficient Learnable Calibration using existing adapters. Their scientific scope and principal performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2 explicitly identifies model size as the assumed key deployment constraint. Section 4.3 adds applicability arguments asserting negligible merging overhead, standard-LoRA latency and throughput, and compatibility with Android AI Core and Apple Intelligence. Existing result interpretations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link, specifies use of the predefined tone-adjustment prompt, identifies comparators using extra compositional data, and describes computing and loading calibrated adapters. These are documentation additions; the PDFs do not establish an actual code or data release.

R1.justification: V2 adds Burke (2023) for Android deployment and removes introductory references to He et al. (2024), Liang Zhang et al. (2024), and Tianyi Zhang et al. (2024). The broader PEFT and model-merging positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The organization changes substantially: scaling, generalization, and three-task analyses move into Appendices D-F; qualitative interpretation is consolidated in Appendix G; and Discussion becomes separate Limitations and Ethical Considerations sections after the Conclusion. Most underlying prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 becomes Figure A4, and Tables 5-6 become Tables A3-A4, alongside other figure and table placement adjustments. Table 2's caption now explains metric abbreviations and the efficiency column. Graphical content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves small documentation ambiguities by identifying baseline supervision, specifying the tone-prompt choice, and explaining deployment assumptions and steps. These changes modestly improve transparency while preserving all empirical evidence. The gains remain limited: the new latency and framework-compatibility assertions are not accompanied by device measurements, and the project link alone does not establish resource availability.
